subject: Vocabulary
description: Latin AQUA (water) and Greek HYDRO (water) roots — aquarium, aqueduct, dehydrate, hydrant, aquatic, anhydrous, hydroelectric.

questions.stem: AQUARIUM literally means a place for what?
questions.explanation: AQUARIUM — etymology aqua (water, Latin) + -arium (place for) = 'a place for water'. So an aquarium is a tank or building containing water habitats for aquatic life. WORD FAMILY (root AQUA = water, Latin): (1) AQUATIC — relating to water; aquatic animals. (2) AQUEDUCT — water channel/bridge for transport (e.g., Roman aqueducts). (3) AQUAPLANE — water-skiing board; also vehicle losing road traction on wet roads. (4) AQUAMARINE — blue-green gemstone (color of sea-water). (5) AQUACULTURE — farming of aquatic organisms (like fish, prawns, seaweed). (6) AQUEOUS — water-based (e.g., 'aqueous solution'). (7) AQUARELLE — watercolor painting. RELATED PARALLEL ROOT: HYDRO (Greek for water) — hydroelectric, hydrant, dehydrate, hydrology, hydrogen ('water-former', because burning H₂ produces H₂O). KEY DISTINCTION between Latin AQUA and Greek HYDRO: both mean 'water'; English uses both interchangeably. AQUA more in everyday names; HYDRO in scientific/technical terms. PYQ FREQUENCY: AQUA root vocab in SSC CGL, CAT, IBPS PO English 1-2× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: rewards systematic root-knowledge.

questions.stem: AQUEDUCT in ancient Roman engineering refers to a:
questions.explanation: AQUEDUCT — etymology aqua (water) + ducere (to lead, conduct) = 'water-leader'. Used by ROMANS to transport fresh water from distant springs/rivers to cities by gravity-driven channels. KEY EXAMPLES: (1) AQUA APPIA (312 BCE) — first Roman aqueduct, by censor Appius Claudius (also built Appian Way). Brought water to Rome from ~16 km away. (2) AQUA CLAUDIA (52 CE) — Emperor Claudius's; ~70 km long; arched portions still standing. (3) PONT DU GARD (France) — UNESCO World Heritage; 50m tall arched aqueduct. (4) AQUEDUCT OF SEGOVIA (Spain) — still in use after 2000 years! ENGINEERING: aqueducts maintained gentle slope (~1:200) over long distances, using arches to maintain elevation. INDIA — TRADITIONAL water-conduction systems: STEPWELLS (baolis, vavs) — Adalaj (Gujarat), Rani-ki-Vav (Patan, UNESCO 2014), Chand Baori (Rajasthan). KARNATAKA HOYSALA tanks. MUGHAL water gardens (Char Bagh) used canals. SIMILAR ROOTS — ducere ('lead'): conduct, deduce, induce, produce, reduce, abduct, viaduct. VIADUCT vs AQUEDUCT: viaduct carries roads/railways; aqueduct carries water. PYQ FREQUENCY: 'aqueduct' in SSC CGL, UPSC History, World History essays.

questions.stem: DEHYDRATE means to remove what from a substance?
questions.explanation: DEHYDRATE — etymology de (away, removal) + hydro (water) = 'remove water from'. Common usages: (1) FOOD PRESERVATION: dehydrating fruits/vegetables (raisins, banana chips, dried apricots) — removes water → inhibits microbial growth. (2) MEDICAL: a dehydrated patient has lost too much body water (causes weakness, dizziness, confusion). (3) CHEMICAL: anhydrous reagents are 'water-free' for sensitive reactions. WORD FAMILY (Greek HYDRO = water): (1) HYDRATE — to add water; or a chemical compound containing water (e.g., hydrated copper sulfate CuSO₄·5H₂O is blue; anhydrous is white). (2) HYDROGEN — 'water-former' (H + O makes water). (3) HYDRANT — public water tap (firefighters). (4) HYDROELECTRIC — using water flow to generate electricity. (5) HYDROLOGY — study of water cycles, rivers, groundwater. (6) HYDROPONICS — growing plants in water-based nutrient solution (no soil). (7) HYDROFOIL — boat that lifts above water on submerged 'wings'. (8) HYDROCEPHALUS — 'water on the brain' (medical condition). EVERYDAY HEALTH: average human needs ~2-3 L water/day (more in heat, exercise). DEHYDRATION at >2% body water loss: noticeable thirst, dry mouth; >5% loss: cardio risk. PYQ FREQUENCY: HYDRO words in SSC CGL, NEET 1-2× per cycle.

questions.explanation: ANHYDROUS — etymology an (without) + hydro (water) + -ous (adjective suffix) = 'without water'. CHEMISTRY: an anhydrous compound is one that lacks water of crystallization (or is water-free). EXAMPLES: (1) ANHYDROUS CuSO₄ (white powder) vs HYDRATED CuSO₄·5H₂O (blue crystals). (2) ANHYDROUS NH₃ (colourless gas) — ammonia in pure form. (3) ANHYDROUS HCl gas vs HCl AQUEOUS (hydrochloric acid). (4) ANHYDROUS NaCl is rare; common table salt absorbs moisture (hygroscopic). (5) ANHYDROUS ETHER, ANHYDROUS ALCOHOL — used in chemistry labs for water-sensitive reactions. WHY ANHYDROUS MATTERS: many reagents react with water (e.g., grignard reagents, sodium metal — react explosively); some catalysts get poisoned by water. ANHYDROUS chemicals stored under DRY ATMOSPHERE (nitrogen, argon) or in DESICCATORS. RELATED CHEMICAL TERMS: (1) HYGROSCOPIC — absorbs water from air (e.g., concentrated H₂SO₄, CaCl₂). (2) DELIQUESCENT — absorbs so much water it dissolves itself (e.g., NaOH pellets in humid air). (3) EFFLORESCENT — loses water of crystallization to air (e.g., washing soda). PYQ FREQUENCY: anhydrous chemistry in NEET, JEE-Main 1× per paper.

options.option_text: An infection caused by water itself

questions.explanation: HYDROPHOBIA — etymology hydro (water) + phobia (fear) = 'fear of water'. CLINICAL CONTEXT: classic LATE-STAGE SYMPTOM of RABIES — patients develop intense fear/aversion to drinking water; even the SIGHT/SOUND of water triggers throat spasms (because rabies virus paralyzes throat muscles). 'HYDROPHOBIA' is sometimes used as a SYNONYM for rabies in older medical literature. RABIES: caused by RABIES VIRUS (Lyssavirus, RNA virus); transmitted by bite of infected animal (dogs in India, bats in Americas). Once symptoms appear, fatality is ~100%. PRE-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS (vaccine) and POST-EXPOSURE PROPHYLAXIS (PEP — vaccine + immunoglobulin) are LIFE-SAVING. INDIA: ~20,000 rabies deaths/year (highest globally); ~99% from dog bites. WORLD RABIES DAY — 28 September. CHEMISTRY USE of 'HYDROPHOBIC': describes substances that REPEL water (oils, fats, waxes, hydrocarbons). HYDROPHILIC = water-loving (sugars, salts, alcohols). Cell membranes have HYDROPHILIC heads (in water) + HYDROPHOBIC tails (away from water) — basis of bilayer structure. PHOBIA suffix: also in CLAUSTROPHOBIA (closed spaces), AGORAPHOBIA (open spaces), ARACHNOPHOBIA (spiders), XENOPHOBIA (foreigners), TRYPOPHOBIA (holes). PYQ FREQUENCY: medical-vocab MCQs in NEET, AIIMS, SSC GA.

questions.stem: HYDROPONICS is a method of growing plants:
questions.explanation: HYDROPONICS — etymology hydro (water) + ponos (work, Greek) = 'water-work'. Method of growing plants WITHOUT SOIL, using mineral nutrient solutions in water. INVENTOR: term coined by W.F. Gericke (UC Berkeley, 1937). ADVANTAGES: (1) ~90% less water than traditional farming. (2) Higher YIELD per square meter (vertical stacking possible). (3) No herbicides/pesticides needed. (4) Faster growth (15-50%). (5) Year-round (climate-controlled). (6) Can grow in cities (urban farming). DISADVANTAGES: (1) High initial setup cost. (2) Requires electricity (pumps). (3) Vulnerability to system failure (no soil-buffer). VARIANTS: (a) NFT (Nutrient Film Technique) — thin nutrient stream over roots. (b) DWC (Deep Water Culture) — roots submerged in oxygenated water. (c) AEROPONICS — roots in mist (NASA used for space-experiments). (d) AQUAPONICS — combines fish farming + plant hydroponics; fish waste fertilizes plants. INDIAN COMPANIES — UrbanKisaan, Letcetra, Future Farms. CROPS: lettuce, basil, strawberry, tomato — best-suited; root vegetables (carrots, potatoes) less suited. PYQ FREQUENCY: hydroponics + sustainable-agriculture in UPSC current affairs, NEET environmental.

questions.stem: HYDROLYSIS, a chemistry term, literally means:
questions.explanation: HYDROLYSIS — etymology hydro (water) + lysis (loosening, splitting, Greek) = 'splitting by water'. Chemical reaction where a compound is BROKEN APART by reacting with WATER. EXAMPLES: (1) DIGESTION: starch → glucose (catalyzed by amylase enzyme + water). Proteins → amino acids (peptidase + water). Fats → fatty acids + glycerol (lipase + water). (2) SOAP MAKING: fats + NaOH/KOH + water → soap + glycerol (called SAPONIFICATION, a hydrolysis). (3) METAL OXIDES + water → metal hydroxides (e.g., CaO + H₂O → Ca(OH)₂ — slaked lime). (4) HYDROLYSIS OF SALTS: solutions of weak-acid+strong-base salts (e.g., Na₂CO₃) become BASIC; weak-base+strong-acid salts (NH₄Cl) become ACIDIC. CONTRAST WITH RELATED REACTIONS: (a) DEHYDRATION SYNTHESIS — opposite of hydrolysis (joins compounds, releases water). e.g., disaccharide formation: glucose + fructose → sucrose + H₂O. (b) HYDRATION — adds water across a double bond (alkene → alcohol). 'LYSIS' suffix = breakdown: ANALYSIS, ELECTROLYSIS, PARALYSIS, PYROLYSIS, CATALYSIS. PYQ FREQUENCY: hydrolysis in NEET, JEE-Main, CBSE class 12 — 1-2× per cycle.
